rationale: Not a consumer. It appeared only because it named the historical namespace twice: in MODULE_ID, and in a second compatibility write of its own object to the legacy unscoped path. Both are gone; the historical object on disk is untouched.
Also not a consumer: it named the historical namespace only in its own MODULE_ID, which became ANALYSIS_ID.

The compatibility layer itself. It names both namespaces deliberately: it is what prefers the normalized path and falls back to the historical one. Five byte-identical copies of that resolution collapsed into it.

Still a consumer, and still reads the same object. It now goes through resolve_spatial_network_object(), so it contains no namespace token of its own and a token search cannot see it. The dependency is visible at R/networks/spatial_network_utils.R instead, and the resolver-caller load test is what keeps it honest.
Same indirection: its literal bootstrap directory and its phantom 01_Tables segment were replaced by resolve_bootstrap_differential_tables(). Before the migration this script could not run at all.
